LESSON: POETRY WRITING – SPOKEN WORD

Grade: Grade 10
Subject: THEATRE AND FILM
Strand: Creating 1.2 Play Writing (25 lessons) ● elements of play writing (story, plot, 
Topic 1.3: Poetry writing – Spoken word
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry writing – Spoken word, part of Creating 1.2 Play Writing (25 lessons) ● elements of play writing (story, plot,  in Grade 10 THEATRE AND FILM.

Key inquiry question: How can spoken word poetry be used to address issues affecting society? 2. Why is spoken word poetry a powerful tool of communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  research to identify the characteristics of a spoken word poem,  read a variety of spoken word poems to help identify

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry writing – Spoken word together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires innovation skills through writing original poems.

● Communication: the learner develops proficiency in language use when writing poems.

● Learning to Learn: the learner acquires new knowledge and skills relevant for continued learning in the course of poetry

writing.

Values:
 Integrity: the learner develops honesty through creation of own works of poetry.

 Patriotism: the learner develops a sense of love for family, community and the country when writing poetry on societal

issues.

 Social Justice: the learner acquires a sense of humaneness by exploring issues affecting the society.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-economic and Environmental Issues: the learner becomes aware of issues affecting society while exploring themes

for writing poetry

● Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner acquires leadership and group dynamics skills during peer review.
